body:
OK, after a long Saturday night, I woke up around 9am and finished putting

up signs directing people to the Sunday location of RCon - the H-wing

Auditorium.  I get there and the tables are not set up so George Gundry,

Mike Publicover, and Johnny Rivera (someone else too...cannot remember)

help me out and we get set up.  People start to come in and then Rich

shows up even though he wasn’t supposed to.  He tells me he calls in sick

;) so he can play!  Great news for me, the more competition, the more fun

it is for me at least to watch.  So after all is said and done prepping

for the tournament, 36 people show up and form 8 different teams of 4.  We

discussed making this event sanctioned but then realized we will

manipulate the pairings and that makes it unsanctioned.  It works out

better for everyone because that way people could have more fun with it.

I know that Bob Caton played a experimental deck 'for the heck of

it because it was non sanctioned.  Plus all the incentive people needed

was the Trophies I had up for grabs.  First place was to get the Endor Set

of foils and once again I used George Gundry's idea of getting posters

signed.  I had 3 up for grabs for this one.  The competition was stiff

with lots of very good players.  After about 45 minutes, two people, Neil

Hoffman and Ivan Turner from Staten Island show up in time for the second

round.  Bart was gracious enough to switch teams to play with them and we

now had 7 teams of 4 and 2 teams of 3.

So in all the event went great with everyone's help. I kind of messed up

the pairing 3 times! ;).  Chris Twig won the overall best score and earned

the Endor Set of foils.  Team Charlie’s Angels won the team tournament with

the trophies and the Team Champ T-shirts.  Afterwards I raffled off 10

support.  I also had 38 more foils to give away that everyone had to pick

face down.



Props-

-Rich Haman helping me with the command cards throughout the entire event

so I would not mess the pairings again ;).

-Bart Robinson for switching teams when part of a team showed up.

-Aaron Kingery and Arthur Wright for helping Rich and I figure the team

tournament results in the 'special room'

-Doug Faust, Ray Bordier for helping throughout the day.

-The people randomly following my arrows on campus thinking I was holding

the 'Open House'

-Everyone for playing!

-Everyone for signing my cards in my Light Side Deck!



Scott Lingrell

summary: Scott Lingrell directed the RamapoCon II team tournament on 7 May 2000: 38 players in 10 teams; Charlie's Angels (Jonathan Chu, Charlie Herren, Steve Brentson, Michael Dalton) won the team title with 14 points, and Chris Terwilliger had the best individual score, 12 (+96).
notes: Tournament director's report (author_played false); Lingrell did not play. Rich Haman helped with the command cards; Aaron Kingery and Arthur Wright helped figure the team results.

Event named 'RamapoCon II Team Championship' from the report's heading 'RCon II Team Championship 5/7/00'; new side event of the existing RamapoCon II hub. Unsanctioned because pairings were manipulated so teammates did not meet.

Team score = sum of the team's three best individual places (e.g. Charlie's Angels 4+3+7 = 14; Team Gout 2+5+22 = 29), as in Decipher's [[Team Event Format]]. Decks were constructed (Premiere - Endor pool).

Field: 36 players in 8 teams of 4 at the start; Neil Hoffman and Ivan Turner arrived for round 2 and Bart Robinson switched to their team. The text then says '7 teams of 4 and 2 teams of 3', but the table lists 10 teams (8 of 4, 2 of 3) and 38 participants; 38 used. Jonathan Chu (d708) counts 9 teams.
Stats given: 51 Light Side wins, 62 Dark Side wins.
Prizes: Chris Terwilliger ('Chris Twig') won the overall best score and the Endor set of foils; Charlie's Angels won trophies and Team Champ T-shirts.

Names mapped: 'Jonathan Chu' -> [[Jonny Chu]]; 'Mike Dalton' -> [[Michael Dalton]] (faramir; a separate [[Mike Dalton]] page also exists); 'Tom Hermley-Keen' -> [[Thomas Hermley-Keen]]; 'Marty Terwilliger' -> [[Marty Terwilliger]] (the hub's standings link a separate [[Martin Terwilliger]] page, likely the same person); 'Art Wright' -> [[Art Wright]] (Team Albany; a separate [[Arthur Wright]] SM page exists, likely the same person); Pete Srodoski, Joe Young, Nathan Brown, Chris Erwin linked to existing pages of those names.
Team name 'Deez****' is as printed (censored in the original).
'Mike D'amboise' written as Mike D'Amboise (the hub's spelling).
Chris Curcio's place printed as '38' (no suffix); recorded as 38th.

discrepancies.text: Lingrell's text says the late arrivals made '7 teams of 4 and 2 teams of 3', but his results table lists 10 teams and 38 participants; Jonathan Chu's report says 9 teams.
